## Propagation lemma
A positive dependence on a subset of signed endpoint coefficient rows excludes every strict word containing the same signed rows, regardless of signs elsewhere. This follows by dotting the exact zero combination with any putative strict separating coefficient vector. Encode each core by the required positive/negative endpoint identities. Split the requirements between the fixed six-pencil prefix (germ masks, with infinity positive) and the eleven singleton choices. The set of singleton binary words containing a core is a subcube: intersect the required singleton bit conditions; unspecified choices remain free. A prefix containing all fixed requirements inherits that subcube. The union of inherited subcubes is a 2048-bit exact rejection mask for these certificates. Intersect it with the direct-capacity predicate by original 47-label union on full positive/negative germ masks, as in R296. All rejected words have an explicit source core from R297. The union is a sufficient rejection set, not a complete algebra test. Keeping source-core indices, prefix identities and exact rejected assignment masks preserves provenance; no sign projection substitutes for the full subsequent capacity observer.

## Reproducer
Extract R247 data, R296 bank, R297 certificate bank from exact pins as in R297. Execute closure(data,bank,cert). Original data and source certificates remain immutable; output masks use singleton order [7,13,17,22,27,30,31,32,33,35,41], bit v is binary assignment v. Core indices zero-based into dictionary below; source triple is R297 prefix index, sixth pattern index and singleton word. Each output row is [prefix index, sixth index, original direct-capacity count, rejected count, rejected bit mask hex, compatible contributing core indices]. Prefixes absent from output have no direct-capacity assignments excluded by this closure.

 for(let k=0;k<data.length;k++){let e=data[k],n=e.normal.map(BigInt),parts=e.normal.join()==="51,2,-1"?[[["1","9","69"],["3","17","187"]],[["2","5","112"],["1","0","51"]]]:e.normal.join()==="17,-1,0"?[[["0","0","1"],["1","17","391"]],[["1","17","69"],["1","17","22"]]]:[e.endpoints];for(let [a,b] of parts){if(dot(n,a.map(BigInt))||dot(n,b.map(BigInt)))throw Error("endpoint");let i=id(a),j=id(b);for(let [u,v] of [[i,j],[j,i]]){let bit=1n<<BigInt(G.length);G.push([u,v,bit]);tag[k]|=bit}}}

 const E=P.map((_,i)=>G.filter(g=>g[0]===i).reduce((m,g)=>m|g[2],0n)),singles=[7,13,17,22,27,30,31,32,33,35,41],S=new Set(singles),row=P.map(([t,B,D])=>[t*t,t*B,B*B,t*D,B*D,D*D]);

 let stats={sourceCerts:cert.length,uniqueCores:cores.length,prefixes:bank.length,positivePrefixes:0,coreCompatiblePrefixes:0,coreMaskVisits:0,capacityAdmissibleRejected:0,fullyRejectedPrefixes:0,partialRejectedPrefixes:0,previousBatchCovered:0,remainingAssignments:0,remainingPrefixes:0,totalAdmissible:0,spotChecks:0};let out=[];
